doc.title: Tim Ries interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 19, 2022

title: Band endings and calling the bridge at The Other Side
summary: Rowe asks about an Eddie Abrams-style ending and calling the bridge; Ries explains keeping tunes concise.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: I wonder if that ending was [scats] because you did that at the end of “Bye Bye”
And I thought wait, what is that, what is that?
Well you know you’re ending the tune and it’s like okay you sound like a band, even though we hadn’t played together as a band, so it was like that makes it sound like —

You know I loved the moment — audience members sometimes don’t know these kind of little things that go on, but I think it was in “Willow Weep for Me” and the form had gone to its conclusion, I think it was an alto solo and I saw you like four beats before you stood up and you said something to Ron and the band went to the bridge instead of back to the top. So I’m pretty sure you said, “Bridge.” And that’s so, I love the onstage etiquette and the learning of the craft and how things work. I don’t have a question except it was cool.

No it’s one of those things because like I played the melody and then Mike played an alto solo and it was like I didn’t need to solo. It was like the song was long enough. I was okay with just playing the melody and then Mike took the solos like hey let’s take the bridge out, we don’t need more than that. And yeah so that’s like, you know, why make a tune ten minutes when it could be — say as much as you need in five.
